parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation; national anti-discrimination law covers gender identity (2016) and hate-crime enhancements exist at entity level, but no documented prosecutions show them operating. Organised anti-LGBT violence is documented (2008 festival storming, 2014 Pride attack despite police coordination, 2023 police-cancelled screenings followed by attacks) — mostly dated, capital-focused, activist-directed. Surveys show broad social hostility (84% opposed to same-sex marriage, 2017), and the leading local monitor records a worsening trend as of 2024. No universal-exposure measures (border, facility, custody, care denial) are documented against visitors, but recourse is thin: protections are largely paper, and a hostile-majority society with weak enforcement leaves the outed traveller with limited remedy. Worst documented feature is tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse plus scattered, partly recent violence — moderately below the acceptance-with-working-remedies tier, above jurisdictions with enforced targeting. Travelling with a minor adds no documented trans-specific exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented — no border or document-mismatch friction recorded for trans visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Resident-facing LGR is vague and surgery-conditioned, but this does not touch a visitor's home-issued documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrests, detention or custody placement affecting trans visitors; same-sex conduct decriminalised (1996/1998).
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Hate-crime enhancements exist but no prosecutions documented, so recourse quality in any police encounter is unknown.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented — no facility, bathroom or ward rules recorded.
federal_state_facilities.protection: National anti-discrimination law (2016) covers gender identity in services on paper.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Enforcement of the 2016 law is not evidenced in the dossier.

care_services.exposure: A 2017 study documents stigma and discrimination from healthcare professionals toward LGBTI patients; clinical settings not reliably neutral.
care_services.protection: Anti-discrimination law formally covers gender identity in services.
care_services.interaction: Visitor needing emergency or routine care may face disclosure risk and discriminatory staff attitudes.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Organised violence against LGBTI public events: 2008 festival stormed with death threats; 2014 Pride organisers attacked despite police coordination; 2023 police cancelled film screenings and activists were attacked. Police failure to protect found by constitutional court (2014).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: First national Pride held 2019 with ~2,000 marchers; hate-crime enhancements in entity codes.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Local monitor's 2024 report records a worsening trend, tempering any reform signal.

minors_guardians.exposure: No trans-specific exposure documented for an adult travelling with a minor; survey hostility toward LGBT children (2015) reflects resident family context, not visitor exposure.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented interaction reaching travelling families.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented organised anti-LGBT attacks, including chasing and beating activists after a 2023 cancelled screening; violence occurred even with pre-arranged police security in 2014.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Constitutional court ruled authorities failed to protect assembly (2014) — accountability finding, but no documented prosecutions of attackers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Attacks target visible activism; ordinary street hostility toward a foreign visitor is extrapolated from hostile surveys, not documented incidents.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No documented prosecutions under hate-crime provisions; monitoring report records worsening trend (2024). Thin-data: no evidence of visitor-facing relief mechanisms.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Statutory anti-discrimination coverage (2016) and entity-level sentencing enhancements exist on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper protections without documented operation hold the jurisdiction a step below the acceptance-with-working-remedies tier.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-A: no visitor-facing register, exclusion regime, or universal-exposure machinery is documented; the traveller's ordinary itinerary faces no documented state lever. Hostile society plus paper-only protections does not reach that tier of operational exposure.

Roughly comparable but lower: 0.55-B documents concrete, recurring border screening exposure with weak remedies. Here no traveller-facing mechanism is documented at all; the exposures are societal hostility and violence against activists, which is tier 3-4, not tier 1-2.

Below 0.75-D: that anchor has operative police review, prosecutions of perpetrators, and protective orders functioning. Here the dossier documents no prosecutions, an unremedied court finding of police failure, and a worsening 2024 climate — recourse is thinner and social hostility broader (84% opposition).

Above 0.45-A: that anchor has a deceptive-presentation statute and routine biometric checks creating universal exposure. This jurisdiction has no trans-specific offence and no documented check regime, so its floor of structural exposure is lower.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime: no criminalisation of same-sex conduct anywhere in the country, an explicit national anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and entity-level hate-crime enhancements — all protective on paper but with no documented prosecutions or enforcement actually operating. Against this, the dossier documents organised anti-LGBT violence (2008, 2014, 2023), a constitutional-court finding of state failure to protect, and broadly hostile social attitudes, with the leading local monitor recording a worsening trend in 2024. No visitor-facing exposures (border, facilities, custody, care denial) are documented, but neither is any working remedy. The worst documented feature is societal hostility with thin recourse plus scattered, partly recent violence — placing the jurisdiction in the upper Elevated Risk band, roughly 0.52, with real uncertainty from thin visitor-specific data.
